pages.title: Pure Matter
pages.text: Distortion strips matter down to what it is. Iron is not iron. It is pure substance wearing iron's shape. I call these $(item)compounds$().

pages.title: Tiers
pages.text: They fall into tiers, each worth three of the one below. I wrote them down as I found them.$(li)Abundant: coal, copper, redstone, lapis$(li)Common: iron, quartz$(li)Uncommon: gold$(li)Rare: diamond, emerald$(li)Ancient: netherite

pages.title: Yields
pages.text: The more an item holds, the more it gives. An ingot or a gem yields one compound, raw ore or a gem ore three, an ore six.$(br2)A storage block gives nine, a raw storage block twenty-seven. Breaking the biggest pieces is always worth it.

pages.title: Essences
pages.text: Living things break down too. Flesh, bone, string, pearls, blaze rods, tears and shells leave $(item)essences$(), on the same tiers, one per drop.

pages.title: Families
pages.text: But matter keeps its $(thing)family$(). Iron becomes gold, flesh becomes bone. Iron never becomes flesh. I tried. I will not write down what came out.$(br2)I suspect other worlds hold matter I have never seen.
